narrative.opening: A storm has sealed Ravenhurst Manor for the night. At the foot of the library stair lies Lord Edmund Ashworth — cold, unmarked, and utterly silent. Six guests remain under this roof, and one of them is a murderer. Two detectives have been summoned. Only the truth will see the doors opened again.
narrative.victim_backstory: Lord Edmund built the Ashworth fortune on shipping contracts and buried more than one rival to keep it. Of late he had threatened to rewrite his will, recall old debts, and expose secrets that several of tonight's guests would kill to keep.
narrative.ending_monologue_template: The truth of Ravenhurst is this: it was {culprit} who, in the {room}, ended Lord Edmund's life with the {weapon}. {culprit} had means, motive, and the one window of opportunity the others did not.

suspects.name: Lady Vivienne Ashworth
suspects.blurb: Composed, black-veiled, and freshly written out of the will.
suspects.note: In mourning black. Has not left the east wing since the doctor came.

suspects.name: Dr. Aloysius Crane
suspects.blurb: Knew every ailment in the house — and every prescription.
suspects.note: Carries his bag everywhere. Called out to sickbeds at all hours.

suspects.name: Mr. Sebastian Vale
suspects.blurb: Edmund's partner in shipping, and lately the loud end of every argument.
suspects.note: A shipping man's grip. Takes the stairs two at a time.

suspects.name: Miss Cordelia Frost
suspects.blurb: Quiet, observant, and owed three months' wages.
suspects.note: Slight enough to pass unnoticed. Sleeps by the nursery.

suspects.name: Capt. Reginald Hawk
suspects.blurb: A sea captain with a war wound and a gambling debt.
suspects.note: An old war wound in the knee. Cannot manage a narrow stair.

suspects.name: Mrs. Agnes Holloway
suspects.blurb: Has run Ravenhurst for thirty years and misses nothing.
suspects.note: Thirty years in this house. Knows every door and every key.

shared.text: Wet mud from the garden path is tracked all the way to the body. Whoever did this had been out in the storm tonight — and not every guest under this roof set foot outside.
There is not a drop of blood on Lord Edmund, nor any burn of powder. No blade was drawn, no poker swung, no shot fired.
The only lamp still burning at the hour of death was in the west wing. The east rooms and the center of the house were dark and locked.

player1_private.text: The cravat was crossed behind his neck and drawn tight, and the knot was pulled hard to the LEFT. Whoever tied it did so with a left hand.
The harbourmaster's log places Captain Hawk at the docks until well past midnight. He could not have been here in time.
No wax was spilled and the brandy decanter is sealed and full. Neither the candlestick nor the brandy touched Lord Edmund.
A fine layer of dust lies undisturbed across the study floor and desk. No struggle happened in that room.

player2_private.text: The killer dined at the table tonight. Dr. Crane was called away to a sickbed before the soup was served and never returned.
Miss Frost was reading to the Ashworth children in the upstairs nursery from nine o'clock until the body was found. Three witnesses agree.
The killer came and went by the narrow servants' stair — the dust on those steps is scuffed, and scuffed in a hurry. Not every guest could take them at that pace.
The brandy decanter stands full and the candlestick is unlit and cold. And the study was bolted from the corridor side all evening — no one was killed behind that door.

red_herrings_p1.text: A maid swears the silk cravat was returned to the tailor weeks ago — surely it could not be the murder weapon.

red_herrings_p2.text: A footman thought he heard Mr. Vale consoling the widow in the lounge at the fatal hour — perhaps the partner is innocent after all.

questions.whereabouts: The library? I've no patience for Edmund's dusty shelves. I kept to my chambers the whole evening.
questions.storm: At my dressing table. I heard the first thunder and thought only that it suited my mood.
questions.knewhim: I knew him as a wife knows a husband who has stopped speaking to her — which is to say, hardly at all, by the end.
questions.lastsaw: At dinner. He did not so much as glance my way, and now he never shall again.
questions.heard: Thunder. Rain. And somewhere below, a door — though in a storm one hears doors that aren't there.
questions.account: I left the table early, sat with my maid while she drew my bath at ten, and did not stir until the screaming began.
questions.suspect: I should sooner ask who among them did NOT have cause. But Mr. Vale shouted loudest tonight.
questions.grievance: Everyone Edmund ever did business with held a grievance. He collected them like debts.
questions.motive: My maid drew my bath at ten and stayed to brush out my hair. She will swear to every minute of it.
questions.gain: Six strangers wearing the manners of friends. I tolerate the captain, pity the governess, and trust none of them — my husband's partner least of all.
questions.quarrel: Raise my voice? We stopped speaking loudly to one another years ago. Silence carries further in this house.
questions.leaving: In this weather? I have not been past the orangery door in a week.
questions.s1_will: A fortnight ago, over breakfast. He told me himself, and seemed to enjoy the telling rather more than the deed.
questions.s1_marriage: As a husband? Not in three years. As a creditor addressing a debt — rather more recently.
questions.s1_maid: Below stairs with the others, I should think. She came up at ten because I rang for her.
questions.s1_veil: I have had black in my wardrobe since my mother died. One does not send out for it, Inspector.
questions.s1_vale: Attentive. Rather more attentive since the will was changed — now that you have made me say it aloud.
questions.s1_debts: I knew that they existed. Edmund did not discuss figures with women. Only consequences.
questions.s1_children: Upstairs with Miss Frost, where they have been every evening since they could walk.
questions.s1_letters: There was correspondence. It concerned the estate. You may read it, if you can find it.
questions.s1_solicitor: I had written to one. I had not yet had a reply. Now, I suppose, I shall not need it.
questions.s1_scream: One of the maids. Ellen, I think. I did not stop to ask her.
questions.s1_hand: She takes the pen in her right hand, without hesitation. My right, as you see. Shall I write something out for you?
questions.s1_garden: I dressed for the evening at seven and not since. Examine the hem yourself, if it will settle the matter.
questions.s1_cravat: He kept six. The grey silk is not on the stand where it belongs — I noticed this morning and thought nothing of it.
questions.s1_lamp: The west. My chambers face the west lawn. I have said so already.

s1_lounge.base: Did he. Behind the veil, something goes very still. Then the footman has better eyes than I do. I do not recall it.
s1_lounge.afterConfront: She sets down her tea very precisely. He was not with me at eleven. I have said that he was, and I ought not to have. I do not know where he was.

shared-1.text: Mud? I have not set foot outdoors in a week.
shared-1.tell: Her composure holds — but she answers before you have finished the question, as though she rehearsed it.

questions.whereabouts: I never entered the house tonight, sir, let alone the library — I was three miles off at a child's sickbed.
questions.storm: Riding through it, soaked to the bone, my bag across my knees. The apothecary will tell you the same.
questions.knewhim: His physician these twenty years. I knew his failing heart better than he did. I did not expect a stranger's hand to stop it.
questions.lastsaw: Midafternoon. I advised him to rest, and he laughed in my face. That was the last of him for me.
questions.heard: Only the village dogs and the storm. I was three miles from this house when it happened.
questions.account: Called away before the soup, gone the whole evening, back only when the bell tolled the alarm. Half the village watched me ride out and ride in.
questions.suspect: I am a poor hand at suspicion. But Vale and Edmund were at each other's throats in the study before I left — make of that what you will.
questions.grievance: The man bred them. I was perhaps the one soul here he paid on time.
questions.motive: Half the village watched me ride out and ride back. The apothecary, the child's mother — a dozen witnesses, and not one of them under this roof.
questions.gain: I am everyone's physician and no one's confidant. They nod to me in corridors and forget me at table. I have always preferred it so.
questions.quarrel: I am his physician, not his equal. One does not raise one's voice to the man who settles the bill.
questions.leaving: To the lodge and back, when they came for me. I went before the soup and returned to find the house full of constables.
questions.s2_sickbed: The gamekeeper's wife, at the lodge. A boy came up with the message during the fish — you may ask him yourself.
questions.s2_return: The child was breech. By the time it was over, this house was full of constables.
questions.s2_health: Failing, and he knew it. His heart. I gave him two years, in September, to his face.
questions.s2_laudanum: Laudanum, digitalis, morphine, and the usual instruments. All accounted for. I will open it for you now if you wish.
questions.s2_body: No wound. No blood. Petechiae about the eyes, bruising at the throat. He was strangled — and not with rope.
questions.s2_prescribe: Her ladyship takes something to sleep. The captain has had morphine for his leg. Neither is any sort of secret.
questions.s2_fees: Not this year. I stopped submitting them in the spring; it seemed kinder than being refused.
questions.s2_secrets: A great many things, none of them mine to hand over unprompted. Ask me a precise question and you shall have a precise answer.
questions.s2_widow: Tired. Sleepless. Nothing that would surprise you in a woman married to that particular man.
questions.s2_time: Between ten and eleven. He was still warm when I reached him, and the rigor had not begun.
questions.s2_hands: He mimes the grip with his right hand, then stops and looks at it. Whoever did this stood behind him and pulled to the left. I could not manage it that way without thinking about it first.
questions.s2_soup: The footman, the boy who carried the message, and the gamekeeper's wife — who was occupied, but conscious throughout.
questions.s2_marks: Something broad and soft. A scarf. A cravat. Something that leaves no line because it does not cut.
questions.s2_mud: Soaked. I walked to the lodge and back in it, and I make no secret of that. But I went out by the front, not the garden.
questions.s2_bolt: Mrs. Holloway draws it. At eight, every evening. I have watched her do it for eleven years.

shared-2.text: Bloodless — strangled, then. I treated bruises on Edmund's throat last month and said nothing. He made me swear to it.
shared-2.tell: The doctor's jaw tightens. There is a secret here — but a kept confidence, not a murder.

questions.whereabouts: The library? No. I told you — the lounge, the whole evening. I'd no reason to go near the place.
questions.storm: In the lounge, consoling Vivienne. The thunder quite frightened her.
questions.knewhim: Partners. Friends, once. Lately he meant to ruin me to save his own skin. But one does not murder over a balance sheet.
questions.lastsaw: At dinner. We parted civilly enough — whatever you may have heard.
questions.heard: Nothing above the storm. Though now you mention it, perhaps a tread on the library stair. I thought nothing of it.
questions.account: Dinner, then straight to the lounge, and there I remained until the alarm. I did not move from that fire all night.
questions.suspect: The captain. He owes money the length of the county, and a debt to a dead man is a debt forgiven. I'd start there.
questions.grievance: Half this house. But grievance and murder are different animals — as a man of your profession surely knows.
questions.motive: The lounge will vouch for me — Vivienne, at least; we sat together by the fire. Take her word and mine and you'll want no other.
questions.gain: Cordial enough. Vivienne leans on me, the captain keeps his distance, the rest I scarcely know. Hardly the nest of vipers you're hunting.
questions.quarrel: Tonight. At the table. Six people will already have told you so, and I shall not insult you by pretending otherwise.
questions.leaving: No. The fire was warm and the weather was not. I had no reason to.
questions.s3_ruin: He meant to hand the creditors my name in place of his own. Yes. I have not pretended otherwise and I do not intend to start.
questions.s3_books: Edmund. Myself. Our clerk in Bristol, who is seventy and cannot see. Why do you ask it in that tone?
questions.s3_shouting: The Bristol contract. Being made the scapegoat for a ledger I never kept.

s3_lounge.base: All evening. Lady Ashworth was there. We sat by the fire and she was frightened of the thunder.
s3_lounge.afterConfront: He does not sit down again. The lounge was dark. I was in it — but the fire was out and the lamp was never lit, and I could not tell you the hour if you asked me twice.

questions.s3_fire: The girl laid it before dinner. After that it burned down on its own. I did not touch it.
questions.s3_widow: Since her husband stopped speaking to her, which is longer ago than you would suppose. There is nothing improper in it.
questions.s3_partner: Friends. Once. Before he learned what could be got by being otherwise.
questions.s3_creditors: Two houses in the City, and a name in Liverpool I would rather not say aloud. Badly enough.
questions.s3_dress: He touches his collar, and lowers the hand again. Nothing. A collar and a stud. I dressed in a hurry tonight.
questions.s3_stair: I know that it exists. I am a guest here, Inspector, not a footman.
questions.s3_collar: The hand stops halfway up. A habit. My collar is too tight — it has been all evening.

s3_cravat.base: The tailor's. Weeks ago, as the maid says. If it is not in this house, then that is precisely where it is.
s3_cravat.afterConfront: His hand goes to his throat, and this time it stays there. Then the tailor has it. Or the maid has it. Or it is lost — things are lost, in a house this size.

questions.s3_west: The lounge is — he stops. You are trying to trap me with the geography of a house I do not live in.

s3_boots.base: In my room. Dry, where I left them. I have not been out of doors since I arrived.
s3_boots.afterConfront: A long silence. ...I stepped out. Briefly. For air, before the rain came on properly. That is all that it was, and I will not have it made into more.

questions.s3_alone: Then she is mistaken, or the hour is wrong, or the footman is. One of the three. I was there.

shared-2.text: Strangled? With what — a scarf? How... intimate.
shared-2.tell: Vale's hand drifts to his own collar, then stops. He sees you see it, and the easy smile does not quite return.

shared-3.text: The west wing? I told you. I was in the lounge all night.
shared-3.tell: He repeats the alibi a half-beat too fast, as if reaching for it.

questions.whereabouts: Only early, to fetch a storybook for the children. Not since supper — the nursery has held me every hour.
questions.storm: Drawing the nursery curtains against it. The little ones fear thunder, you understand.
questions.knewhim: I am owed three months' wages. Beyond that, Lord Edmund scarcely troubled to learn my name.
questions.lastsaw: At supper, and briefly. I take my meals with the children, not the family.
questions.heard: Only the storm, and one of the children crying out from a dream. Nothing from below.
questions.account: The nursery, the nursery, and the nursery — with three children and the night-nurse to swear to every hour of it.
questions.suspect: I am paid to watch children, not my betters. But Mrs. Holloway was abroad in the corridors at odd hours tonight.
questions.grievance: Unpaid wages are a reason to stay and be paid, sir — not to kill the man who owes them.
questions.motive: The night-nurse and three children, sir. I was not out of their sight long enough to boil a kettle, let alone do murder.
questions.gain: I keep to the nursery and the servants' table. The guests are names I'm bid not to trouble. Only Mrs. Holloway ever speaks to me kindly.
questions.quarrel: Once — when the wages were three weeks late rather than three months. He did not care for it. I did not repeat it.
questions.leaving: No. I was with the children from nine, and children do not permit you to wander.
questions.s4_wages: Twice, politely, in writing. He replied once — to say that governesses who could count might do better teaching arithmetic.
questions.s4_nursery: From nine until the screaming. Two hours of Mr. Dickens, which the children will confirm and resent.
questions.s4_witness: Both children, and Ellen, who brought the milk up at half past nine and stayed to listen.
questions.s4_observe: That Mr. Vale looks at her ladyship as though she were already a widow. He has done for months.
questions.s4_position: No. It never was. That is rather what a position like mine is.
questions.s4_children: More than they ought. Children hear everything through a floor.
questions.s4_widow: Kindly — in the way one is kind to furniture one has grown used to. I do not complain of it.
questions.s4_letters: Once, to the post, for her ladyship. I did not read the direction, and I would not tell you if I had.
questions.s4_leaving: I had answered an advertisement in Bath. The reply is in my room. You may have it.
questions.s4_noise: Everything. Doors, mostly. And tonight a door at the garden end that has no business opening after dark.
questions.s4_hand: She holds up her right hand, quite steady. This one. I am right-handed — and so are both children, if that is any use to you.
questions.s4_alibi2: Master Thomas, Miss Beatrice, and Ellen the housemaid. Ask them separately, Inspector. I would much rather you did.
questions.s4_vale: I came down at nine for the milk. The lounge door stood open and the room was empty — I remember it because the fire had burned so low.
questions.s4_mud: I heard the garden door. I did not see who. After nine and before the screaming, and that is all I will swear to.
questions.s4_dark: I carried a candle down from the nursery. The whole middle of the house was black. I remember thinking it unlike Mrs. Holloway.

shared-3.text: The lamp in the west wing? The children and I were nowhere near it.
shared-3.tell: She hesitates — she saw something from that nursery window, and has not yet decided whether to tell you.

questions.whereabouts: Those library stairs are beyond this leg of mine. I've not seen the room in months, storm or no.
questions.storm: On the dock road, cursing my horse and the rain in equal measure. The harbourmaster logged the hour.
questions.knewhim: Old friends, Edmund and I. He lent me money I could not repay — and a friend who lends is a friend you cannot easily refuse.
questions.lastsaw: Before I rode out, near eight. He clapped me on the shoulder and told me to settle my account. I never did.
questions.heard: Nothing. I was a mile of wet road away by then, as the harbour ledger will confirm.
questions.account: Out to the docks before nine, back past midnight — and this leg of mine won't let me hurry either way.
questions.suspect: Vale's temper. I've watched men hang for less than the things he said across that dinner table tonight.
questions.grievance: Owed money sours a man, certainly. But a debt outlives the lender — it merely passes to the estate.
questions.motive: The harbourmaster's ledger has my name and the hour beside it. I was a mile of wet road from this house when it happened.
questions.gain: Vale and I keep our distance — oil and water, that pair. The doctor's decent. The widow I've known since she was a girl. The rest are furniture to me.
questions.quarrel: Often. We were old friends, and old friends shout. It means rather less than you are hoping.
questions.leaving: I came IN from outside, Inspector. I had been at the harbour since the afternoon.
questions.s5_debt: Four hundred, to a man in Portsmouth who does not take excuses. Edmund knew. Everyone knew.
questions.s5_forgiven: A debt to a dead man is a debt to his estate — and his estate keeps better lawyers than he did. It is worse, not better.
questions.s5_docks: Past midnight. The harbourmaster keeps the log, and he keeps it honestly. I have cursed him for it before now.
questions.s5_wound: Stairs. Narrow ones especially. I came up the main flight tonight and it took me a full minute.
questions.s5_war: With him. Two years off the Cape. He was a braver man then than he later became.
questions.s5_ship: A third of her. He bought in when I could not pay for a refit, and he never once let me forget the arithmetic.
questions.s5_vale: Because he is the sort who is charming to you in front of other people. I have met a hundred of him at sea.
questions.s5_drink: Two. Perhaps three. Not enough to matter, and not enough to forget — before you ask me that next.
questions.s5_temper: Entirely earned. But I shout at men to their faces. That is rather the point of shouting.
questions.s5_sea: A bowline, if I wanted him to live. He pauses, and his eyes narrow. You did not ask me that lightly.
questions.s5_log: Cottrell, the harbourmaster, in his own hand. He signs everything twice. He is that sort of man.
questions.s5_stair: Not tonight. Not last night. Not in four years. I should have had to be carried down it.
questions.s5_mud: At the front door, with the footman, where a guest leaves them. I did not come through any garden.
questions.s5_cord: Something soft, then. Cord bites, and leaves a line you would see. Whatever went round that man's throat was cloth.
questions.s5_lounge: I passed it as I came in. The door was ajar, and the room was dark and empty. I remember thinking it a waste of a good fire.

shared-3.text: I never reached the west wing — those stairs are beyond me now.
shared-3.tell: He taps his bad leg for sympathy, but his eyes flick away the moment he says 'never'.

questions.whereabouts: I passed its door on my rounds and found it dark. I'd not have gone in — the library is the family's room, not mine.
questions.storm: In the kitchen, seeing the fires banked and the candles counted. I felt the whole house shiver with the first clap.
questions.knewhim: Thirty years in his service. I knew his habits better than his wife did, God forgive me for saying so.
questions.lastsaw: I carried up his evening brandy at nine. He waved me off without a word. That was the last.
questions.heard: A gentleman's tread on the servants' stair — and gentlemen do not use the servants' stair. It stayed with me.
questions.account: Every corridor in this house passed under my eye at one hour or another. I am never not seen, and I see everything.
questions.suspect: Mr. Vale took the servants' stair tonight. I'd not have credited it of him — but I know what these old eyes saw.
questions.grievance: Plenty held grievances. I held my tongue thirty years; I'll not pretend the others were so patient.
questions.motive: A housekeeper is seen by all and vouched for by none, sir. I was everywhere this evening, and so, I suppose, nowhere. Ask the footmen.
questions.gain: I serve them all and befriend none — thirty years teaches the difference. I'll say only this house holds more grudges than guests.
questions.quarrel: Thirty years, and not once. It is not my place, and he was not a man who invited it.
questions.leaving: To the kitchen yard for the bins, before the rain came on properly. Not since.
questions.s6_years: Him. He was always a hard master, but this last year he became a frightened one — and frightened men are worse.
questions.s6_keys: Myself, his lordship, and the butler. And the butler has been in Scarborough since Tuesday.
questions.s6_staff: Ellen, the two kitchen girls, the footman and the boot boy. All below stairs, all evening, all accounted for.
questions.s6_dinner: Her ladyship, Mr. Vale, the captain, and his lordship. Dr. Crane was called away before the soup. Miss Frost dines upstairs.
questions.s6_cleaning: The halls at six, before the guests came down. They were spotless when I left them, Inspector. Spotless.
questions.s6_gossip: That there is something in it. I do not repeat servants' talk — but you have asked me plainly, and I will not lie to you.
questions.s6_wages: Miss Frost. Three months of them. And she has never once complained where the children could hear her.
questions.s6_laundry: Shirts, collars, cuffs, cravats. Counted out and counted back. I know what every gentleman in this house owns.
questions.s6_doors: The garden door and the study, at eight, by me. The front stays on the latch until the last guest is in.
questions.s6_edmund: Hard. Not cruel, until lately. I have buried a better master, and I have buried a worse one.
questions.s6_mud: After eight, or I should have seen it on my round. It was not there when I drew the bolts. It was there when they screamed.
questions.s6_missing: A cravat. Grey silk. Mr. Vale's. It has not come through my laundry and it is not on his stand — and I count, Inspector. I have counted for thirty years.
questions.s6_lamps: I put out the east and the centre myself. The west was her ladyship's, and one does not put out a lamp her ladyship is sitting beside.
questions.s6_bolt: I did. At eight, as I have every night for thirty years. It was still drawn when the constables came.
questions.s6_tailor: Nothing has gone to the tailor this month. I send the parcels myself and I keep the book. Whoever told that maid otherwise was mistaken.

shared-1.text: Mud in the hall? I'd have had it scrubbed within the hour. I never saw it — which means it was tracked in very late indeed.
shared-1.tell: She is the only one here who seems to be helping you. Whether she is helping, or steering, you cannot yet say.

contradictions.note: Vale places himself in the lounge all evening. Miss Frost came down at nine and found it empty, the fire burned low.
Vale places himself in the lounge all evening. Captain Hawk passed an open door and saw a dark, empty room.
Vale says the cravat went to the tailor weeks ago. Mrs. Holloway keeps the parcel book and says nothing has gone this month.
Vale names Lady Ashworth as his alibi. She does not recall sitting with him at the fatal hour.
